environment: Stand-in cart page with the example's pricing, headless Chrome at 1200×720
summary: We clicked through the cart like a shopper would: 6 of 6 checks passed, and the checkout check was skipped because the demo has no backend.

scenarios.title: Under $50, the banner says how much is left, and adding an item unlocks free shipping
scenarios.why: If the amount is wrong, shoppers either chase a goal they already hit or pay shipping they shouldn't.

steps.action: Open a cart with a $22.50 tote and a $15.00 mug
steps.expected: "Add $12.50 more to get free shipping." and $5.99 shipping

steps.action: Add a second mug with the + button

scenarios.title: A cart of exactly $50.00 ships free
scenarios.why: The boundary is where an off-by-one bug would charge shipping on a qualifying order.

steps.action: Open a cart that adds up to exactly $50.00

scenarios.title: A coupon that takes the order under $50 brings shipping back
scenarios.why: Free shipping counts what the shopper pays after the coupon, not the list price.

steps.expected: "Add $5.00 more to get free shipping.", $5.99 shipping, $50.99 total

scenarios.title: Gift cards don't count toward free shipping, and a gift-card-only cart ships nothing
scenarios.why: Gift cards are emailed, so counting them would hand out free shipping on small physical orders.

steps.action: Open a cart with a mug, a notebook and a $25.00 gift card
steps.expected: "Add $22.50 more to get free shipping." even though the subtotal is $52.50

steps.action: Remove the mug and the notebook
steps.expected: No banner and $0.00 shipping, because nothing ships

scenarios.title: Bulky items keep their delivery fee when shipping is free
scenarios.why: Free shipping covers the standard fee only; dropping the bulky fee would lose money on every lamp.

steps.action: Open a cart with a $54.00 floor lamp that has a $15.00 bulky fee
steps.expected: "You've got free shipping! Bulky items still have a delivery fee." and $15.00 shipping

scenarios.title: Orders outside the US pay international shipping and see no banner
scenarios.why: Free shipping is US-only, so other countries must not be promised it.

steps.action: Switch "Ship to" from United States to Canada
steps.expected: The banner disappears and shipping is $19.99

scenarios.title: Checkout charges the same shipping the cart shows
scenarios.why: If checkout priced shipping on its own, shoppers would see one number and pay another.
scenarios.note: This demo has no checkout backend, so there was no order to place.

steps.action: Place an order for the $37.50 cart through the checkout API
